text: The Patriots survived a late-inning scare from the Jets on Sunday, grinding out a 26-19 victory behind Drake Maye's three touchdown passes to improve to 2-0 in the AFC East, but the win came with some concerning developments on the injury front and a notable regression from one of their offensive stars. A.J. Brown, returning from a four-week absence following a right high ankle sprain, looked decidedly out of sync in his first game back, dropping a career-high three passes that underscored just how much rust he's accumulated on the sidelines. The injury troubles compounded when Romeo Doubs took a hard fall after hauling in a 42-yard touchdown pass from Maye with 4:10 left in the first quarter—a spectacular catch that came at what may have been a significant cost. Still, the Patriots are operating under Mike Vrabel's clear philosophy that there's no apologizing for wins, and a 2-0 division record heading into the second half of the season isn't something anyone in New England's locker room is going to complain about, even if some of the supporting evidence suggests there's real work to be done before the next slate of opponents.
